steps.name: Dimensionar
steps.task: Read the request, the project sheets and the product notes. Say how big the work is (S, M or L) and why, which open epic it belongs to or whether it needs a new epic of at least 8 stories, and what decisions nobody has taken yet. For follow-ups of a finished story, each follow-up is size S unless it hides a decision. Then validate the request for discovery: for every project it touches, read the "Discovery" field of its project sheet; a website (seo) lists the rules of rules/discovery/seo.md the work touches, an app (aso) lists none while rules/discovery/aso.md has no rule, and a project whose sheet has no Discovery is "unclassified": never guess, put the question in "openDecisions".

steps.name: Partir
steps.task: Write the epic and split it into user stories, each with its project, size and acceptance criteria, and each story into tasks. No story may be L. An epic is the unit of a commit: it holds at least 8 stories, usually 10 to 25, grouped by outcome. Read the backlog and the open issues first and reuse an open epic of the same project or theme, adding the new stories to it, instead of opening a new one; only the standing "Maintenance of <project>" epic may hold fewer. For follow-ups of a finished story, drop what is already filed and make each new follow-up a task under the story "Keep <project> in step with its code" of the epic "Maintenance of <project>", for the project it changes; reuse that epic and story while they are open.

steps.name: Escrever as issues
steps.task: Write every issue in English exactly as it will be published: one epic, its stories and their tasks. Never mention agents, skills, LangGraph, or who does a task vs. an agent in the issue text. Give each a short key (Epic, S1, T1), its kind, title, body with the acceptance criteria, size, repository (owner/name) and the key of its parent. To change an issue that already exists, put its link in "issue"; to reshape an epic, reuse its id and keys. List in "closedIssues" the issues that stop making sense. The flow engine keeps the draft in the backlog. For follow-ups of a finished story or a settled decision task, put that story's or decision task's issue in "closedIssues". Every rule the size step listed in "discoveryReview" for the draft's project appears by its id, such as (SEO15), in the acceptance criteria of at least one story.

steps.name: Aprovação
steps.task: Read the draft with read_backlog and show the user every issue exactly as it is stored, grouped by size, and the issues that will be closed. Wait for an explicit yes and quote the user's exact words in "userWords". Never infer a yes.

steps.name: Criar as issues
steps.task: Read the approved draft with read_backlog. Create each issue with gh, or update the one in "issue", using exactly its stored title, body, issue type and labels. Link stories to the epic and tasks to their story as sub-issues, close the issues in "closedIssues", and hand back the link of every key. The flow engine records the links in the backlog.
